title: DNS and Content Delivery: Route 53 and CloudFront

questions.prompt: How does a CDN like Amazon CloudFront reduce latency?

options.text: It caches content at edge locations near users, serving from a nearby site instead of the origin
It makes the origin server's CPU faster
It stores data only in one Region

questions.explanation: CloudFront caches content at edge locations worldwide, so requests are served from a location near the user, cutting latency and offloading the origin.

questions.prompt: You want the zone apex (example.com) to point at a CloudFront distribution. What do you use?
questions.explanation: CNAMEs can't sit at the zone apex; a Route 53 alias record points the apex directly at AWS resources like CloudFront or a load balancer, at no per-query cost.

questions.prompt: Match each Route 53 routing policy to its purpose.

pairs.right: Send users to the lowest-latency Region
Switch to a secondary when a health check fails

questions.explanation: Latency routing optimizes speed, weighted splits traffic, failover provides HA/DR with health checks, and geolocation routes by where the user is.

questions.prompt: CloudFront caches content at ____ locations around the world to serve users nearby.
questions.explanation: Edge locations are the globally distributed sites where CloudFront caches and serves content close to users.

questions.prompt: After a deploy, users still see old content through CloudFront. Why, and what fixes it?

options.text: CloudFront is broken; recreate the distribution
Cached objects are served until their TTL; create an invalidation or use versioned filenames
Route 53 caches the whole website permanently

questions.explanation: Caching is why a CDN is fast, but stale objects persist until TTL expires; an invalidation (or versioned asset names) forces the new content.

questions.prompt: Which can serve as a CloudFront origin? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: CloudFront can fetch from S3, an ALB/EC2, or any HTTP origin. A CloudWatch alarm is monitoring, not a content origin.
